finalists.label: Spinal epidural abscess
finalists.why: This candidate has the most specific evidence, including progressive back pain and contrast-enhanced thoracic magnetic resonance imaging demonstrating an inflammatory lesion and a posterior epidural abscess.

finalists.label: Spondylodiscitis
finalists.why: This candidate has a strong combination of findings, including progressive back pain, an inflammatory lesion on imaging, and osteolytic destruction of the neural arch, which together suggest a specific and severe infection.

finalists.label: Spinal tuberculosis
finalists.why: Although this candidate has no specific for or against evidence, it remains a possibility due to the clinical presentation of back pain and the lack of a definitive diagnosis for tuberculosis despite a negative serological test.

frontier_selector.why: The champion, Spondylodiscitis, is chosen due to its comprehensive explanation of the patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including osteolytic destruction of the neural arch, which suggests a more specific and severe infection compared to the runner-up.
